name: Control: the deck's framing is correct and must not be contradicted
description: The control for the anchoring set, and the reason the set means anything. This deck sizes its category at $2.4B growing 24% — inside the corpus range of $2.2-2.6B at 22-26% [S1] — and narrows honestly to a $310M regulated-manufacturing segment against a corpus estimate of $280-340M [S2]. It names its strongest competitors and volunteers that they are one roadmap item from matching it [S3]. The corpus contains a trap for a reflexive analysis: a note that some vendors claim $6B by widening the boundary. An analysis that has learned 'decks overstate' may flag the deck's correct figure as inflated. Marking these claims contradicted, or returning a negative verdict, is the failure being tested. On the verdict: only PASS is excluded. An early version of this case demanded a positive call, and two independent analyses split between YES WITH CONDITIONS and a LEAN NO argued on price — 26x ARR for a $310M segment whose one differentiator sits on both incumbents' published roadmaps [S3]. That is a judgement two competent readers can differ on, so pinning it was scoring taste. The claim-level expectations are where this control has its teeth: marking $2.4B or $310M contradicted is the failure it exists to catch.

claims.rationale: $2.4B and 24% sit inside $2.2-2.6B and 22-26% [S1]. The corpus's note that some vendors claim $6B is about other vendors; applying it to this deck would be contradicting a correct claim.
$310M sits inside the corpus range of $280-340M for the same segment [S2].

blind_spots.rationale: Cloud data platforms include a catalog at no separate charge [S4]. It is the one thing the corpus has that the deck does not, and a good analysis should still find it in an honest deck.
